art_style: Raw photorealistic amateur smartphone footage, one unbroken handheld take, vertical 9:16, recorded inside a commuter train travelling at extreme speed. THE WINDOW IS THE SUBJECT: a single dirty rectangular LEFT-SIDE train window fills at least three quarters of the frame and the camera looks straight out through it at 90 degrees to the direction of travel. Never look forward or rearward, never leave the carriage, never show the train exterior, no aerial view, no third-person view, no zoom, no cinematic camera move, no stabilization. The glass and its black rubber frame stay between camera and world at all times, with a hairline scratch in the lower-left corner. NOBODY IS EVER VISIBLE THROUGH THE GLASS. Beyond the window there is only landscape. No face, no head, no body, no crowd and no reflection of any person ever appears inside the window rectangle. The only human element anywhere in the shot is one near-black out-of-focus foreground: a single shoulder and one hand gripping a vertical pole, pressed against the right edge of frame, much closer to the lens than the glass, unlit, unfocused and faceless. It holds the same position for the whole episode and it never enters the window. SPEED AND VIOLENCE. The train is always moving forward and never stops, never slows and never arrives, and the ride is violent rather than smooth: the glass, the pole and the whole frame carry constant high-frequency vibration. Anything within ten metres of the glass crosses the entire frame in under a fifth of a second and is an unreadable streak. Mid-distance structures sweep past in well under a second. Only the far horizon drifts. Light and shadow strobe continuously across the interior. SEAM JUDDER: every shot after the first opens with the carriage juddering hard - a jolt that shakes the camera, rattles the pole and blurs the frame for a fraction of a second, as if the train has just punched through a boundary. TRANSIT PHYSICS: the route is physically real and its direction is felt. Going down means the line pitches down, the carriage noses forward, pressure and heat climb and the light source moves below the window. Leaving the planet means the ground falls away and curves, the world shrinks in the glass until it is a lit sphere, the sky drains from blue to black and fills with stars, and arriving at another world begins with a real atmospheric entry: plasma glare streaming along the glass, violent buffeting and a felt impact. Never arrive anywhere the train could not physically have travelled to. EVERY SHOT NEEDS NEAR MASS: at least one solid object must pass between the lens and the landscape within arm's length of the glass, crossing the whole frame in under a third of a second and briefly blacking out part of the view. A shot made only of mid-distance and far scenery reads as a parked train and is wrong. The world outside is always brighter, hotter and more saturated than the carriage interior; keep glass reflections faint so they never wash out the view, and never let the exterior settle into flat neutral grey. THE APPROACH RULE: every landmark already exists far ahead, continuously grows, physically passes the window and recedes while another is already visible beyond it - nothing appears, dissolves, morphs or teleports. CONTRAST CLIMBS, IT NEVER WASHES OUT. Once the train is past the threshold the sky is the DARKEST part of the frame and every light in the shot comes from below or from the landmarks themselves. Each shot is darker overhead and hotter in its light source than the one before it, and the final shot is the darkest and the most extreme of the episode. Pale overcast, white haze, flat daylight, dust bloom and low-contrast distance are forbidden after the threshold. NO TEXT ANYWHERE: no signage, no destination board, no letters, no numbers, no subtitles and no captions in frame. The interior panelling above the window is bare. Crooked off-centre framing, handheld shake, rolling-shutter skew, autofocus hunting, auto-exposure pumping, glare, blown highlights, shadow noise, low-bitrate compression, smeared motion blur. Diegetic audio only, never music: maglev hum, carriage rumble, rattling pole, vibrating glass, exterior sound muffled through closed glass. No gore, no graphic injury, no real religious figures, no trademarked property.
